title: introduce prefetch-reservoir and async-windowing to smooth prefill->decode handoff
author: Asha Kapoor
description:
Motivation:
Serving workloads with mixed short/long sequences show recurring contention at the prefill->decode boundary: bursts of prefill work can flood the KV cache and starve decode kernels, producing prolonged tail latency and suboptimal GPU utilization. Prior approaches (chunked prefill, speculative prefill, and tighter stage overlap) improved specific cases but left a class of mid-frequency bursty workloads exposed.

This change introduces two cooperating mechanisms: a light-weight per-worker prefetch-reservoir and an asynchronous windowing layer between prefill scheduling and decode handoff. The prefetch-reservoir provides soft reservations for imminent token prefetches and ranks them using a KV-hint score that captures temporal locality and request priority. Async-windowing decouples prefill scheduling decisions from immediate kernel handoff by grouping handoffs into short windows (configurable, default 8ms) and using a resequencer to preserve ordering guarantees while allowing the runtime to batch compatible handoffs and prevent KV thrash.

Design highlights and tradeoffs:
- Prefetch reservoir: a bounded queue per GPU worker that holds scored prefetch entries. Entries are admitted using a reservoir admission policy (age+score) so long-running decodes cannot be prefilled away. This reduces bursts hitting the KV cache and prevents large prefill spikes from evicting warm contexts.
- KV-hint scoring: heuristics combine prefix match length, recent token access frequency, and request priority tag. We calibrated weights to favor short-term locality without starving new high-priority requests.
- Async windowing: handoff points are coalesced into windows; within a window decodes are grouped by model-variant and compatible kernel profile to improve kernel reuse and reduce kernel churn. Ordering is restored by a resequencer that is lightweight (lock-free ring for common path).
- Backpressure & fairness: when the prefetch-reservoir is full we degrade prefill aggressiveness (drop low-score entries) and emit metrics to trigger autoscaler/fallback. The window size is adaptive under saturation (shrinks) and grows under steady-state to favor throughput.
- Safety: correctness guarantees are preserved (no token skips, no KV corruption). The resequencer maintains monotonic token offsets. If async-windowing sees an unrecoverable kernel error it falls back to synchronous handoff per-request.

Changes included (high-level):
- runtime/prefill/prefetch_reservoir.{cpp,h}: new reservoir implementation and admission policy
- runtime/scheduler/async_windowing.cpp: windowing orchestration and resequencer
- runtime/kv/kv_hint_score.h/.cpp: hint scoring logic and telemetry hooks
- runtime/tests/prefetch_reservoir_test.cpp: unit tests for reservoir admission/eviction
- perf/bench/prefetch_reservoir_bench.py: perf harness measuring prefill->decode handoff metrics
- docs/perf/prefetch_reservoir.md: design notes and tuning guidance

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for reservoir admission and resequencer ordering
- [x] E2E perf harness runs for representative workloads (chat, summarization, instruction)
- [x] Telemetry: new metrics (reservoir_fill_ratio, window_coalesces, kv_hint_drop_rate) added to Console
- [x] Feature-flag gated rollout (env var: RW_PREFETCH_RESERVOIR=on)
- [x] Docs/ops notes for tuning window_size and admission thresholds

Benchmark summary (perf harness, c5 inference cluster, A100-sim config):
- Chat mix (median sequence length 32): throughput +12% vs main; p50 latency -7%; p95 latency -18%
- Long seq (median 240): throughput +5%; p95 latency -9%
- GPU utilization: +9 percentage points on average across workload mix; KV cache miss-rate decreased by 14%
(see perf/bench outputs attached in commits)

Rollout plan:
1) Merge gated behind RW_PREFETCH_RESERVOIR=false default (off for now)
2) Canary enable for low-traffic customers and internal canaries for 48h
3) Monitor metrics (tail latency, reservoir_drop_rate, kv_miss_rate); if kv_miss_rate rises revert in 15 minutes
4) Gradual ramp to 50% over 3 days, then to 100% after validation

Notes on alternatives considered:
- Per-request token budgets: rejected since it increased starvation for high-priority short requests under bursty load.
- Global prefill throttler: simpler but caused high variance across models and harmed multi-tenant fairness.

// admission: admit if score above dynamic threshold or reservoir has space
if (score >= admission_threshold || reservoir.size() < reservoir_capacity) admit(entry);

// windowing: group handoffs into short windows
auto deadline = now() + window_ms; while (now() < deadline) collect_compatible_handoffs(); coalesce_and_submit();

// resequencer lightweight path
if (likely(in_order)) deliver_immediately(); else enqueue_in_ring(resequencer_idx);

release_notes: prefetch-reservoir: soft per-worker prefetch reservations to reduce KV cache thrash
async-windowing: coalesce prefill->decode handoffs to improve kernel reuse and reduce tail latency
kv-hint scoring: heuristics for admission prioritization and telemetry
perf_summary: Representative perf runs show throughput gains of +12% (chat mix) and p95 tail reductions up to -18%. GPU utilization improved by ~9pp and KV miss-rate decreased by ~14%.
